newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European stocks rise, sterling strong.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European stocks rise, sterling strong.

text.p: European bourses rose on Thursday morning, with London's FTSE-100 index rebounding from a sharply lower open after the previous day's British budget sparked interest rate jitters.

As British stocks trekked over both negative and positive ground on fears of an UK interest rate rise, sterling welcomed prospects of higher rates and stayed on its upward path. The pound lingered near its five-year high against the mark and its five-month high versus the dollar.
The FTSE-100 index swiftly tumbled more than 50 points at the open as the market priced in at least a 25- to 50-point rate hike at next week's monetary meeting.

"In the budget, whilst the Chancellor talked about coming down on demand, he didn't hit the consumer that hard, and the reaction to that is that base rates will have to go up, probably next week, and by at least 25 basis points," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson's Philip Isherwood.

But just before midmorning, London stocks rebounded on bargain hunting and on perceptions that a rate rise next week would not portend a new uptrend in rates. Financials and utilities, seen as the most sensitive to interest rate changes, led British stocks up .
British government debt prices, an indicator of interest rates, also recovered from session lows.
German and French stocks were more focused on Wall Street's jump overnight after the Federal Reserve left U.S. rates unchanged, as expected.
The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average surged in the final hour of trading to close up 73 points at 7,795.
Germany's DAX index reached an all-time high at the open, with traders looking to break a key psychological level at 4,000.
But DAX gains could be limited, depending on the Dow's reaction to key monthly jobs and inflation data due later in the day.
If U.S. data show any inflationary signs, world stocks could encounter a bumpy ride in the afternoon.

Paris stocks were up, but traders said activity was choppy. They said shares were mostly higher in line with Wall Street, but uncertainty over the government's economic and budget policies was keeping a lid on prices.
"We are near the all-time high, and the prospect of higher taxes for companies is clearly negative. The market is fragile," a broker in Paris said.
On Wednesday, France's Socialist government said it was considering boosting corporate taxes to ease budget woes.
In currency markets, the dollar held narrow ranges above 1.75 marks, a just below 40-month high, and 114 yen in early trading as the market awaited the U.S. data.
A Reuters survey forecasts June non-farm payrolls to gain 220,000 after May's 138,000 rise. Average hourly wages were seen jumping 0.4 percent.
"It will be very quiet....waiting for the minutes of the last Fed meeting and the unemployment figures, which could give the market a bit of a lift," said Peter Wood, Bank of Boston dealer.
After U.S. data are released, traders said dollar trading could quite as dealing winds down before the long, Fourth of July weekend there. U.S. markets are closed on Friday.
CURRENCIES AT 0910
The dollar was at 114.40 yen and 1.7543 marks compared with 114.44 and 1.7515 in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0910 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 5.2 points at 4,756.60.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 19.20 at 2,928.65.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 29.49 at 3,884.25.
PRECIOUS METALS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
Gold opened in London at $332.50 an ounce, up from $332.35 at Wednesday's close. Silver opened unchanged at $4.66.
